reply_text:
㊥ (has the move to the JVM happened?) Half of it has. PR #68 moved turn recording, sending to 象 and collecting readings into the JVM, keyed by session and turn id. But it still stores everything as files in the same directory, and your Emacs doesn't use it yet. So the record and its reading are not evidence yet. Shall I start on that?

㊢ (what's there) The JVM routes `/api/alpha/xiang/turns…` are built and running, and the Matrix bridge path already uses them. Two things are not done:
1. **Emacs still records the old way.** Nothing in `futon3c/emacs/` calls those routes. Emacs writes `turn-*.json` itself, sends readings through `agency_send.py` and collects them through `turn_dispatch_reap.py`. The two paths share a directory but are two separate implementations.
2. **The store is still files.** `turn_store.clj` deliberately kept the files under `~/.emacs-graph/session-turn-analysis/` the same, so `turn_frames.py`, the stepper, `xlate.py census` and feed.html would keep working unchanged. The only link to futon1b is the operator turn's `evidence_id`, which the record carries.

㊭ (order of work)
1. Point Emacs at the JVM routes: record when you send, report what happened when the reply ends, and let the JVM send to 象 and collect the reading. `小象` stays local, as you say. `象-off` then has to reach the JVM too, since otherwise turning it off in Emacs would no longer stop anything.
2. Have `turn_store` write the record and its reading as futon1b evidence entries citing the operator turn's `evidence_id`, and keep writing the files until the readers move.
3. Move the readers (`turn_frames.py` first, since the stepper depends on it) onto evidence, then retire the files.

Each step is one handoff with a review before the next. I'd send them to Kimi or Zai if they have usage, otherwise Codex. A bulk backfill of the 2,049 existing readings would need throttling, because large bulk writes have flooded futon1b before.

🈯 ("You can fix") I took this as "push", which seemed to fit best after my last turn. The three commits are now on GitHub, and futon3c master matches origin. If you meant the two kernel problems from the P24 experiment, say so and I'll do those too: agreements refused without seat info, and delivered work still showing as owed.

previous_reply_acts.text: (cause and fix) `M-x turn-stepper` opened from its cache whenever one existed and never fetched again. The cache only refreshes by itself when a 象 reading lands while the stepper window is visible. So after two days closed it stood at 182 frames, while `turn_frames.py` had 286. Now opening shows the cache straight away and fetches fresh frames behind it. The fix is in `futon3c/emacs/turn-stepper.el`, committed as `5eab74eb`. I reloaded it, opened the stepper from this buffer, and watched the frame count go from 182 to 281.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (why 281, not 286) The stepper leaves out your newest turns that 象 hasn't read yet. Your last five turns, from "Hm... turning off the Emacs path…" (22:35) onwards, have no reading yet. Several fall in the time 象 was off, so they were recorded but never sent to 象, and they won't get a reading. Turns sent since you ran `象-on` should get one, and the stepper refreshes as each reading lands while it's open.
